correctness.rationale: The no-cancellation integral recurrence and exact formula Q_{n+1}=(u_{n-1}+v_{n-1})²/gcd(h,u_n) are derived and checked. The criterion that Q_{n+1} is a square exactly when gcd(h,u_n)=1 is proved for odd prime factors and separately at 2. Every odd-p obstruction is a first hit of zero by z+z^{-1}. At each nonempty depth level, the sign/inversion Klein-four action contributes four points except at the first level and possibly the level containing ±1. Thus a hit at depth k forces at least 4k-4 different nonzero points, yielding k<=(p+3)/4, and Q-index <=(p+7)/4. Prime 2 can act only at index 2; primes 3 mod4 never act. h=x0=5 has Q3=9/5. Code checks 135621 relevant finite-field starts and 4240 direct recurrences, but proof is universal.

originality.rationale: The accepted claim is the explicit universal prime-quarter time deadline and its supporting fourfold level-count lemma, not the known density or periodicity of square failures. Direct statement-and-implication comparisons with the new reciprocal-sum paper, an earlier starting-value law, and 2014 finite-field dynamical work did not locate this bound. value.rationale: The motivating theorem bounded only the number of exceptional terms along each sequence. The new inequality supplies a closed numerical last-failure index valid simultaneously for every positive starting integer and every power of a fixed h, without requiring enumeration of a finite-field graph. Fourfold orbit counting improves the elementary p-sized search horizon by a factor of about four, with equality at p=5. This is a structural uniform cutoff for a natural arithmetic recurrence, not a new table of small cases or a restatement of the known density law.
